findings.title: Requirement/scenario coverage registry is materially incomplete and its claims are false
findings.issue: PAI.md states PAI.requirements.json 'maps all 69 binding spec IDs and ten verbatim §13.2 scenarios', but the supplied file contains 20 requirement entries and 2 scenarios. Missing bindings include SEC-01/SEC-03/SEC-04, OPS-02, COST-02, MODEL-01/02, and 8 of the 10 required §13.2 reference scenarios, so PA-01's 'эталонные сценарии' deliverable and full-product coverage are unmet while the design asserts otherwise.
findings.fix: Expand the registry to the complete binding spec-ID set and all ten verbatim §13.2 scenarios with per-slice paths/test nodes/roles/evidence, or correct the claim and record every uncovered ID/scenario as an explicit unresolved gap; re-verify with an independent mapping check.

findings.title: Machine registry defines only 7 of the declared 32 packets
findings.issue: PAI.md calls PAI.design.json 'the draft machine registry for all 32 packets', but only PAI-00..06 exist in it. Requirements and scenario nodes reference PAI-07..29 (e.g. tests/test_pai_end_to_end.py, PAI-25/28 cutover, PAI-21/26 deletion), which have no allowed/forbidden files, change budgets, verification argv, rollback, or dependencies. Cross-phase interfaces consumed by this design (ingress wiring, scheduler, effects, migration/cutover) are unconstrained.
findings.fix: Either define PAI-07..29 packets (files, budgets, verification, rollback, dependencies) in the registry, or explicitly scope this feature design to PAI-00..06 and stop asserting 32-packet coverage; record the remainder as separately planned, unreviewed scope.

findings.title: PAI-00 can edit the review policy, receipt-producing reviewer tooling, and publication receipts
findings.issue: PAI-00's allowed_files include docs/REVIEW_POLICY.md, tools/run_codex_role.py, tools/opencode_role_review.py, tools/mimo_code_review.py, tools/finalize_opencode_design_reviews.py and their tests, plus 'bounded publication receipts' — the exact chain that manufactures the independent-review evidence this programme depends on. No gate requires independent diff review of changes to runner/receipt parser code before those receipts are trusted.
findings.fix: Move review-tooling and REVIEW_POLICY changes into a separate maintenance packet reviewed by an independent party; forbid PAI-00 from editing receipt-producing/parsing code or review policy without explicit approval, and require hash-bound re-validation of existing receipts after any such change.

findings.title: Declared verification policy is not enforceable by the registered commands
findings.issue: PAI.md requires 'missing files/skip are failures or unknown evidence, never PASS', but all registry verifications are plain `pytest -q ...` with expected_exit_code 0 — skips and missing optional nodes still exit 0. PAI-01's only check (tools/check_pai_plan.py) is structural, is itself owned/editable by PAI-00 (see related finding), and evidently does not detect the false 69/10/32 coverage claims in this very packet.
findings.fix: Register strict commands: enumerated node IDs with fail-on-skip/missing (`--strict-markers`, no `-q`-only), explicit counts, and a plan checker asserting markdown↔design.json↔requirements.json consistency and full ID/scenario coverage; have that checker independently verified and pinned.

findings.title: Durable effect state machine conflicts with the ADR dispatch protocol
findings.issue: PAI.md declares durable transitions prepared -> dispatching -> succeeded/known_no_effect/unknown, but ADR-013 has the second transaction 'mark dispatch_started' and hold row locks through the transport call and settlement — meaning `dispatching` is only committed together with the outcome, so it is never durably observable and a crash mid-call leaves state `prepared`. Recovery treats both as unknown, so safety holds, but the state contract, PAI-04's 'attempt fixed before fake provider effect', and operator-facing status disagree.
findings.fix: Specify exactly when dispatch_started commits (before the call, in its own transaction, with the same lock order), which states are durable, and that recovery/reporting treat prepared and dispatching identically as potentially-unknown.

findings.title: Lock scope of shared budget windows during transport is undefined
findings.issue: The final-effect transaction reacquires grant/proposal/reservation rows and holds locks through a bounded (10s) transport call plus settlement. If request/job/day/month budget window rows are in that lock set, unrelated reservations sharing a day/month window block for the call duration and a hung transport can starve the single effect executor's connection; no lock/statement timeout or over-bound behavior is specified.
findings.fix: Define the minimal lock set and window granularity, per-transaction lock/statement timeouts, separate effect pool sizing, and the outcome when the bound is exceeded (state remains prepared/unknown, no automatic retry, owner-visible status).

findings.title: Blocking granularity of unresolved unknown/prepared effects is undefined
findings.issue: 'Unknown or any unresolved prepared effect blocks re-dispatch' does not say whether it blocks only that effect, that job, that operation group, or the whole scope/queue. Without a bound this can head-of-line block unrelated work; with PAI-03's unknown-spend settlement it also determines how long budget stays conservatively consumed.
findings.fix: Specify blocking granularity (effect/operation group/job), the owner-visible status and cancel path, and that unrelated jobs/scopes continue within their own budgets and consents.

findings.title: PAI-05 and PAI-06 can run in parallel over the same storage modules and contracts
findings.issue: Both depend only on PAI-03/PAI-04 yet both write `src/prm/storage/**` and share job/object-ref contracts (conversation object_refs feed the PAI-06 job payload). No ordering or file-level partition is declared, so concurrent slices can conflict or diverge on repository semantics.
findings.fix: Serialize PAI-05 before PAI-06, or partition `src/prm/storage/**` modules and repository ownership per slice with explicit shared-interface ownership.

findings.title: Runtime interface contract omits mandatory operations
findings.issue: The listed interfaces cover begin/enqueue/claim/checkpoint/cancel/authorize_and_reserve/prepare_effect/dispatch/reconcile, but the design mandates 5s heartbeat lease extension and lease-expiry recovery/quarantine, and job payloads bind input object/version/digest. No heartbeat/extend, recover/expire, or digest-check signature or invariant is given, so fencing semantics for stale workers are only partially specified.
findings.fix: Add heartbeat(lease, token, generation) -> extended/stale, recover/expiry rules (safe compute checkpoints only, quarantine of versions, no effect reclaim), and require checkpoint/dispatch to verify the payload digest before committing.

findings.title: PAI-04 writes outside the declared code topology
findings.issue: PAI-04 allowed/expected path `src/assistant/prm_post_answer_actions.py` sits outside the declared layout (src/prm domain, src/prm/storage, src/prm/runtime, src/bot transport) and outside PAI-01's stated file areas; no design or ADR defines this boundary, its ownership, or why action logic is not in src/prm.
findings.fix: Relocate the module under src/prm (or record an ADR entry naming src/assistant as an explicit boundary with owner, tests, and permitted callers) before PAI-04 implementation.
